title: Sikandar Raza surpasses Babar Azam in unwanted T20I record after golden duck
content: Raza was dismissed for a golden duck by India pacer Yash Thakur, taking his tally of ducks as T20I captain to seven. Only former Australia captain Aaron Finch has more ducks as captain in the format, with eight. Babar Azam and Rohit Sharma are next on the list with six each.

title: CJP's win fuels call by 'E20 Janta Party' for no-ethanol option
content: A new E20 Janta Party has emerged, demanding consumer choice for 100% petrol. This group seeks the resignation of Nitin Gadkari, the transport minister. Transporters are supporting this campaign, planning a march to Parliament against E20 petrol. The party advocates for transparent fuel labelling and data publication. They are not seeking subsidies but consumer choice and clear information.

title: Sergey Brin says he fought Google's ban on engineers using Gemini
content: Google co-founder Sergey Brin discovered Gemini on an internal coding tool prohibition list. He spent weeks attempting to remove this restriction himself. After failing to resolve the issue, Brin approached CEO Sundar Pichai for assistance. Pichai proved supportive and helped lift the outdated restriction on Gemini usage. This incident highlights how internal rules can lag behind company AI strategies.

title: Jeff Bezos ex-wife MacKenzie Scott helped write a 'donation playbook' for Snap founder
content: Snap co-founder Evan Spiegel and Miranda Kerr have donated $550 million to erase medical debt. This significant contribution will benefit over 261,000 Californians facing financial hardship. The donation follows a philanthropic model pioneered by MacKenzie Scott. Undue Medical Debt will administer the funds, targeting vulnerable residents statewide. This initiative aims to unburden families from unpayable medical expenses.

title: Can China’s electric rocket launcher make Musk’s chemical rockets obsolete?
content: China has successfully achieved the recovery of an orbital-class rocket booster, similar to the reusable models pioneered by SpaceX. Recently, they conducted a test on electromagnetic launch systems, focusing on the initial lift-off phase. This innovative technology aims to lessen the dependency on chemical propellants, potentially making space launches more affordable and enhancing payload capabilities. Such advancements highlight China's escalating aspirations within the global space sector.

title: 4 moose released in 1904 became 200,000 and changed Newfoundland forests
content: A century after just four moose were released in Newfoundland to attract hunters, the introduced animals transformed the island's forests and wildlife management. Their population grew to nearly 200,000 before habitat damage triggered declines. A new management plan explains how science is now helping keep moose numbers in balance with forests, public safety and long-term ecosystem health.

title: ‘Panda of the sea’ fish returns to Hong Kong after DNA gives it away
content: A recent study has confirmed the presence of the rare Chinese bahaba in Hong Kong's waters through genetic material extracted from seawater. Nicknamed the 'Panda of the Sea,' this critically endangered fish had evaded scientific capture for over ten years. Researchers utilized cutting-edge environmental DNA technology, revealing traces of the fish's DNA across various western bays, thereby advancing non-invasive methods for marine population monitoring and conservation.

title: Amid billionaire exodus, NYC's Mamdani tells $5M homeowners: Check your mail
content: New York City's mayor is implementing a new tax on expensive second homes. This tax aims to fund essential public services across the city.  The city is currently experiencing an outflow of high-income residents to other states.  Meanwhile, major companies like Airbnb are expanding their presence in New York City.  These developments highlight ongoing economic shifts within the metropolitan area.

title: Sacrifices of Kargil heroes will inspire generations: PM Modi
content: Prime Minister Modi highlighted India's growing defense production and export capabilities.  He mentioned recent defense technology tests and missile agreements with Indonesia.  The nation also paid tribute to soldiers who sacrificed lives during the Kargil war.  Defense Minister Rajnath Singh contrasted India's innovation with Pakistan's focus on terror.  India is consistently moving towards new heights in defense and international cooperation.

title: From Jantar Mantar to Parliament: Govt, oppn brace for fight over NEET row, other issues
content: As the monsoon session reconvenes, tensions rise again over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal. Opposition factions are determined to maintain pressure on the administration following significant protests. Prime Minister Modi has introduced reforms for examinations and established a dedicated task force for student welfare. In response, Rahul Gandhi is targeting the government over police conduct. The government aims to introduce a bill designed to eradicate malpractice in examinations.

title: Taylor Swift, Travis Kelce's $2m gift moves families of fallen NYC heroes
content: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's generosity has brought heartfelt reactions from families of fallen New York City heroes who have long relied on Answer The Call for support. Widows and children shared emotional messages, with one saying, "I am in tears," while thanking the couple for their kindness. The donation is part of the couple's wider charitable efforts ahead of their wedding, but what touched these families most was the reassurance that the sacrifices of their loved ones will never be forgotten thanks to the couple's $2 million gift.

title: How Stephen Curry’s biggest setback changed his NBA career forever
content: Stephen Curry's journey to NBA greatness began long before his iconic 54-point game at Madison Square Garden in 2013. From the frustration of being overlooked by major college programs to finding his path at Davidson, Curry's biggest setback became the foundation of his remarkable career. As the first active NBA player to receive a dedicated exhibit at the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, his story is a reminder that patience, self-belief and perseverance can transform rejection into lasting success, inspiring generations of basketball fans around the world.

His vehicle struck a crowd at the Christopher Street Day celebration, leading to one death and sixteen injuries.

The party ended its demonstration in good faith after a key demand was met.

title: US, Russian astronauts return safely to Earth after 8-month mission aboard ISS
content: A joint US-Russian crew safely returned to Earth after completing their mission. They spent over eight months aboard the International Space Station orbiting the planet. This safe return highlights continued space cooperation between the two nations despite geopolitical tensions. The crew landed in Kazakhstan after their successful 241-day journey. Another crew arrived at the ISS earlier this month for their own mission.

title: Gold's next test: Fed verdict, crude oil and geopolitical tensions in focus
content: Gold and silver prices are set for a week driven by major events. The US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision will be a key factor. Geopolitical tensions involving Iran and crude oil price movements also impact markets. Investors will monitor US economic data and central bank announcements globally. Bullion is expected to remain range-bound as traders watch these developments.

title: Patrick, Brittany Mahomes turn family pain into food allergy awareness
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes attended a back-to-school event with FARE just before Chiefs training camp, continuing their advocacy for food allergy awareness. The couple's mission comes from personal experience after their children, Sterling and Bronze, were diagnosed with food allergies. Brittany has previously shared the frightening details of Bronze's severe allergic reaction and how it inspired the family to help others. Here's how Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are using their platform to support parents and create safer environments for children with food allergies.

title: Why India's tiles and marble industry isn't worried about the Red Sea crisis
content: India's tiles and marble sector anticipates continued growth, supported by strong domestic housing demand. Rising freight costs and supply chain issues present short-term challenges for manufacturers. Robust residential real estate transactions indicate sustained consumer interest in premium housing options. Expanding commercial projects and infrastructure development will further boost material consumption. Industry stakeholders remain optimistic about long-term growth driven by urbanization and construction.

title: RDJ's role led to Chris Evans' return as Captain America for 'Avengers: Doomsday'
content: In an exciting turn of events, Chris Evans will reprise his beloved role as Captain America in the highly anticipated Avengers: Doomsday. After careful consideration and rejecting countless offers for eight years, Evans chose to come back, motivated in part by Robert Downey Jr.'s role as Doctor Doom. He aims to make Steve Rogers’ story impactful as the film introduces returning X-Men stars, scheduled for release on December 18.

title: 'Hang culprits': Mother of NEET aspirant who died says Pradhan's exit not enough
content: Parents of Akanksha Chaturvedi demand justice and compensation after her suicide following the NEET-UG paper leak. They express dissatisfaction with Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation from his post. Akanksha's mother called for stricter punishment for those responsible for the examination controversy. Her father stated that his daughter aspired to become a doctor and serve the nation.

title: ‘Responsible for brutal assault on students’: Oppn turns heat on Shah, seeks resignation
content: Opposition parties will intensify their Parliament attack on the government. They are demanding Home Minister Amit Shah's resignation over police action. This action involved students protesting the NEET paper leak issue. The government is also set to introduce amendments to the anti-paper leak law. Questions are also being raised about a key higher education secretary appointment.

title: Thousands of Himachal teachers launch indefinite hunger strike against School Complex System
content: Thousands of primary teachers marched to Shimla after a 15-day foot journey. They launched an indefinite relay hunger strike against the new School Complex System. Federation leaders claimed the policy weakened primary education and affected teacher deployment. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu assured that most demands were accepted. Teachers will continue their agitation until changes are formally notified.

title: Nepal to require Everest climbers to prove experience first
content: Nepal has introduced new rules for climbing Mount Everest. Aspiring climbers must now summit a 7,000-meter peak first. This aims to reduce overcrowding and improve climber safety on the mountain. Experienced mountaineers support these new regulations for better preparation. Indian climbers will need to plan multi-year expeditions for their Everest dreams.

title: India’s first hydrogen-powered train saves 3,200 litres of diesel; Delhi route tests next
content: India's first hydrogen train has traveled over 1,200 kilometers during trial operations. This indigenous project has already saved over 3,200 liters of diesel fuel. The train generates electricity using hydrogen fuel cells, releasing only water vapor. Dedicated hydrogen storage and refuelling facilities have been established at Jind. Further trial runs are planned for the Delhi route to support zero-emission rail transport.

title: ‘No law bars eating chicken over Ganga’: SC judge flags delayed bail at NLIU lecture
content: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan expressed concern over shrinking public space for dissent in India. He noted that courts often grant relief belatedly and impose restrictive bail conditions. These conditions can discourage citizens from exercising their fundamental right to express views. Justice Bhuyan cited cases where individuals faced prolonged jail time for minor offenses. He stressed the need for critical examination of judicial decisions to improve the system.

title: 'This is a new subject for me': Pralhad Joshi after taking charge as education minister
content: Pralhad Joshi has taken charge as the Union Education Minister. He is reviewing the ministry's functioning and familiarizing himself with its operations. Joshi expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for this new responsibility. This change follows Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation from the Union Council of Ministers. The ministry change occurs amid student protests over examination irregularities.

title: Romania shoots down third suspected Russian drone in three days, summons Moscow's envoy
content: Romania shot down a drone entering its airspace over the Black Sea. This marked the third such interception in as many days. President Nicusor Dan condemned these repeated violations as intolerable and unacceptable. Romania summoned the Russian ambassador to protest these airspace breaches. Investigations are ongoing into the drone incidents and border tensions are high.
